FX-SPLIT-001.says: The settings as they start: from 25, 50 to 75, 50, split 50, wider than the drawing: the middle torn wide open, transparent from top to bottom between the points, the ends kept.

FX-SPLIT-002.says: Split 4: a gap 4 pixels wide at the middle of the middle row, closed at 4, 5 and 12, 5, the band pushed up and down and squeezed into the 4 pixels each side; columns left of 4 and right of 12 untouched.

FX-SPLIT-004.says: Both points at 50, 50: the drawing, untouched.

FX-SPLIT-005.says: From 50, 10 to 50, 90, split 4: torn down the middle column, the stripes pushed left and right.

FX-SPLIT-006.says: From 10, 10 to 90, 90, split 3: torn along the diagonal.

FX-SPLIT-007.says: Split keyed from 0 at frame 0 to 8 at frame 4, linear: frame 0 the drawing, frame 2 FX-SPLIT-002.

FX-SPLIT-008.says: Point B keyed from 25, 50 at frame 0 to 75, 50 at frame 4, split 4: frame 0 nothing torn, frame 4 FX-SPLIT-002.

FX-SPLIT-009.says: FX-SPLIT-002 moved three pixels right: the same, moved; nothing grows.

FX-SPLIT-010.says: Split eased from 0 at frame 0 to 1000 at frame 4 on a curve that overshoots: at frame 2 it would pass 1000 and is held there.

FX-SPLIT-011.says: FX-SPLIT-002 with the points swapped: the same picture.

FX-SPLIT-012.says: From -50, 50 to 150, 50, split 6: the points off the drawing, the tear running right across it, 6 pixels wide at the middle.

FX-SPLIT-013.says: Split 1001, above 1000. The file is read, the effect is kept as written and left out of every frame, with a warning.

FX-SPLIT-014.says: Split -1, below 0. The file is read, the effect is kept as written and left out of every frame, with a warning.

FX-SPLIT-015.says: Point A at 1001, 50, past ten widths. The file is read, the effect is kept as written and left out of every frame, with a warning.

FX-SPLIT-016.says: Point B at 50, -1001, past ten heights. The file is read, the effect is kept as written and left out of every frame, with a warning.

FX-SPLIT-017.says: Split keyed to 1500 at frame 4. The file is read, the effect is kept as written and left out of every frame, with a warning.
